Photograph: Thames Valley police/PA UK criminal justice Burnham ‘increasingly confident’ PC Harper’s killers will not get early release Prime minister says he has asked justice secretary to push through measures to increase the number of prison places Peter Walker and Caroline Davies Tue 11 Aug 2026 07.09 EDT First published on Tue 11 Aug 2026 03.52 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Andy Burnham has said he is increasingly confident he can adapt the early release scheme for prisoners to exclude the killers of PC Andrew Harper and other serious offenders, saying he understood and shared the public’s concern about their potential release. Writing on Facebook , the prime minister said on Tuesday he had asked the justice secretary, Alex Norris, to rapidly push through a series of measures to increase the number of prison places, requiring fewer people to be released early to free up room. Downing Street said on Monday that there was no feasible way of exempting just a handful of prisoners from the scheme to block the release of Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were sentenced to 13 years for Harper’s manslaughter. The pair were due to be freed in January under plans to release about 5,000 people early under an emergency plan to create more space in the prison estate in England and Wales. Exemptions were made for those convicted of rape, serious child sexual abuse and grooming offences, but not manslaughter, prompting pressure to block the release of Harper’s killers, including from police and his family. View image in fullscreen PC Andrew Harper. Photograph: Thames Valley police/PA No 10 had already changed stance, saying Burnham has asked Norris to “work through further options to keep a greater number of the most serious offenders in prison, including the killers of PC Harper”. In his Facebook post, Burnham said the early release scheme could be mitigated by expanding prison places in three ways: removing foreign offenders more quickly; finding a way to release lower-risk prisoners stuck in jail on indeterminate sentences; and “making greater use of the entire prison estate including using the female estate for male offenders”. He wrote: “I am increasingly confident that a more focused approach along these lines will allow us to reduce the number of people released early and, in the case of the most serious offenders like those convicted of the killing of PC Harper, prevent their early release altogether. “In advance of the justice secretary’s proposals being presented to parliament, we will seek to engage other political parties in discussions with the aim of gaining the widest possible public and political consensus on the approach being taken.” Burnham wrote that he understood “the depth of public concern about the potential early release of those involved with the killing of PC Andrew Harper – and I share it”. “I fully appreciate the anguish of Andrew’s family and, more broadly, of all those victims and their families who may see those who caused them such harm not serve their full sentence. It is incumbent on me as prime minister to do everything within my power to minimise that possibility. And I am determined to do so.” Speaking later during a visit in Derbyshire, Burnham said he would prefer to not release any prisoners early, and that he was aware of the public feeling over the issue. “It’s my job to speak up for the public on this issue,” he said. “I take that duty very seriously indeed, and I’m confident that there’s more that can be done, and will be done to address public concern.” He added that No 10 officials had been in touch with Harper’s family on Monday night, and Norris was “in regular touch as well”. Harper, 28, was fatally injured when he got caught in a strap attached to the back of a car and was dragged down a country road as the killers fled the scene of a quad-bike theft in Sulhamstead, Berkshire, in 2019. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters Preview latest after newsletter promotion Cole and Bowers, two of three men sentenced over the police officer’s death, are due to be released halfway through their 13-year sentences, having been convicted of manslaughter in 2020. A petition demanding an intervention has nearly 900,000 signatures. View image in fullscreen The driver Henry Long got a longer sentence and does not qualify for early release. Photograph: Thames Valley Police/PA Prison Service officials have warned Burnham that changing the terms of the prisoners’ early release scheme so that those convicted of manslaughter, such as Cole and Bowers, remain in jail would mean further early releases would be needed within 18 months. Governors told the Guardian the prime minister’s decision last week to exempt rapists and serious child sex offenders would force thousands of sentences to be recalculated in haste and could lead to the mistaken early release of some prisoners. The early release changes were part of the Sentencing Act passed earlier this year that cut the minimum amount of time many offenders would have to spend in prison. The third man jailed for the manslaughter of Harper – the vehicle driver, Henry Long – was given a longer jail term of 16 years. Because he received what is called an extended determinate sentence, he cannot be considered for this early release scheme. Harper’s mother, Debbie Adlam, told the BBC Radio 4 Today programme on Tuesday the debate over the killers’ release had been a “rollercoaster” but that she had heard directly from Downing Street “so we’ve now got a little bit of hope”. Speaking of others affected by the early release plans, she said: “We are not alone on this journey. It’s the world that we have been thrown into. You want what is right for your family member. They’ve lost their life through somebody else’s actions. You have to be their voice. “We are not asking for a special case for Andrew here. We are not stupid, we know it needs to be done the right way.” Explore more on these topics UK criminal justice Andy Burnham Prisons and probation Angela Rayner Alex Norris Labour Police news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story PM urged not to change scheme to stop PC Andrew Harper killers’ early release What could Andy Burnham do to block early release of PC Andrew Harper’s killers? https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/16/russ.text: Russia used Anthropic's Claude AI model to accelerate cyber-espionage operations against Ukrainian and European government targets, run disinformation campaigns in Africa and Moldova, and develop targeting software for autonomous kamikaze drone swarms, the US company said in a report published this month.Anthropic said it had blocked all malicious activity identified in the report, used the findings to strengthen its security systems, and shared the information with government bodies and industry partners.In one major case, a hacking group designated GTG-20006 used Claude to automate operations against more than 20 organisations, including government ministries, defence and intelligence agencies, embassies, think tanks and defence-industrial companies, Anthropic said.Ukraine was the primary target, with suppliers of military drone technology and their supply chains also among those attacked. The group also targeted Middle Eastern and Asian government departments with links to maritime activity.Anthropic said GTG-20006 is linked to Midnight Blizzard, a hacking group Western intelligence assessments attribute to Russia's foreign intelligence service SVR.The group used Claude across a range of operational modes: as an engineering assistant for writing malware, phishing kits and surveillance tools, as an executor of commands on victims' networks, including collecting credentials and extracting data under human direction, and in fully autonomous operations with minimal human oversight.Disinformation in the CAR and MoldovaWorking alongside investigators from the All Eyes On Wagner project, Anthropic identified and removed an account operated by a Russian-speaking individual in Bangui who was running a disinformation operation for Radio Lengo Songo, a station set up and financed in 2017 by the Kremlin-run mercenary Wagner group.The operator prepared daily pro-Russian content for the station in coordination with Russian state outlets RT, Sputnik Afrique and TASS, and with the local "Russian House" cultural centre — part of a network Russia uses as a political and influence hub abroad.Content consistently promoted the CAR government and Wagner, and attacked France and domestic opposition figures, according to the All Eyes On Wagner investigation.The operation was designed to appear locally run, with one person coordinating output while contracts, scripts and publications were presented as the work of a Bangui-based radio station.Anthropic investigators identified the individual through invoices for a Claude subscription issued in central Madrid.The operator was linked to Africa Politology, aka "The Company," the information and political technology arm of the African Corps — the successor to Wagner in Africa — which is reportedly controlled by the SVR.In Moldova, a former regional head of the Russian state-run Sputnik media network used Claude as a content-production tool, adapting news, polling data, and opposition material to fit pro-Kremlin narratives, Anthropic said.Autonomous swarm drone warfareAnthropic identified and shut down a group of Russia-linked developers who used its Claude Code tool to write software for kamikaze drones, including an autonomous targeting system tested on real hardware.The developers trained AI models on footage from combat operations in Ukraine and used a fixed location in the Donetsk region as a demonstration strike target.The project's stated goal was a fully autonomous swarm of FPV kamikaze drones.Anthropic linked nine accounts involved in the project to a regional Russian university and a federal research centre connected to the Russian Academy of Sciences, without naming either institution.Claude is officially unavailable in Russia, with access to Anthropic's website and API blocked and Russian bank cards not accepted for payment. The developers bypassed these restrictions by routing traffic through commercial virtual private servers (VPNs).

https://www.dailystar.co.uk/news/latest-.text: Russia has said it will destroy the capital city of a NATO country if war breaks out as tensions skyrocket within Europe. Nikolai Patrushev, a top aide to Russian President Vladimir Putin threatened to destroy Warsaw, Poland if war with NATO broke out. "If Poland enters into military action against Russia , our country will use the entire arsenal of forces and means at its disposal, and Warsaw will cease to exist within two or three days," Patrushev told Russian news outlet Argumenty i Fakty. His threat comes after Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said NATO could "quite quickly" defeat Russia if attacked by Moscow. Poland joined NATO in 1999. NATO, a 32-member alliance, was formed in 1949 to counter the risk of Soviet attack. It now focuses protecting ally counties by promising that an attack on one member is considered an attack on all. Speaking at the annual Yalta European Strategy conference in Kyiv, Sikorski said, "If Russia attacked us and we took our gloves off, I think we would defeat Russia quite quickly." He added that NATO's airpower superiority over Russia was overwhelming and spoke of the 2,500 military aircraft at the alliance's disposal. Patrushev called Sikorski's comments an "amateurish assessment of our country's military might." He also said that Russia was not using "their full potential" in their war against Ukraine . However, Patrushev reiterated reassurances out of Moscow that his boss has no intention of going to war with Europe, Metro reports.

https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2.text: Just as the leaders awkwardly posed for the family photo, we got a line in the Dutch media, via Kyiv Independent, that the Dutch embassy in Kyiv was damaged in a Russian drone attack on the Ukrainian capital. The Rotterdam-based Algemeen Dagblad stresses it’s not clear if the embassy was the intended target or just accidentally damaged as part of a broader attack. But, in what is a curious coincidence, the incident comes just a day after a rather provocative message from Russia. On Wednesday, the Russian embassy in the Netherlands asked if The Hague was “openly joining the conflict” in Ukraine (Europe Live, Wednesday) after a Dutch-headquartered company, Destinus, said its missiles were used in a Ukrainian attack on the Kerch Bridge in Russian-occupied Crimea. I have reached to the Dutch ministry of foreign affairs to get their line on the incident. Will let you know when we hear back from them.

Audi, BMW, Ford, Opel and Volkswagen are all in IG Metall's sights, as are shipyards in northern Germany. Companies say they cannot afford to pay wage increases and will have to slash benefits, site upgrades and hundreds of thousands of jobs in the automotive, electrical and mechanical engineering and metal production sectors. They are instead offering a phased increase of 1.3% for 2028 — Germany's current inflation rate is hovering around 3%. It is the first time the union and its 3.7 million members have turned to 24-hour strikes in eight years and they are hoping the move will offer them some leverage when collective bargaining talks begin next week. IG Metall's northern coastal representative Daniel Friedrich said Friday: "Our members stand united behind our demands. On Monday, we will continue the 24-hour strikes at more companies." Edited by: Sean Sinico https://p.dw.com/p/5PhQb Skip next section Qatar to invest €15 billion more in German defense tech, says Merz 11/20/2026 November 20, 2026 Qatar to invest €15 billion more in German defense tech, says Merz Jon Shelton German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Friday announced that Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani had pledged €15 billion ($16.5 billion) in new German defense and technology investments. During a Berlin press conference with the emir, Merz said, "This strengthens both of us, particularly in future technologies such as artificial intelligence , semiconductors and aviation." The Qatar -Germany collaboration is aimed at improving security and defense projects that also include defending against cyberattacks, with Merz saying, "We are particularly open to new partnerships in the defense industry." That cooperation comes as both nations look to beef up defenses amid regional conflicts with global consequences . The chancellor and the emir also stressed the fundamental importance of diplomacy in the resolution of conflict, with the two leaders' focused largely on Iran and the Middle East — and the need to get the flow of shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz closer to pre-war levels. The emir called for deescalation, saying, "We are convinced that true political resolution is the only way to achieve lasting peace." Merz added that the two agreed on the war in Ukraine , saying: "Russia must stop its time-wasting diplomatic games. Moscow has to finally sit down for real peace negotiations." Merz was straightforward on Iran, saying Germany wants peace in the Middle East because it needs affordable energy. He later called out Russian maritime marauding on the Black Sea, labeling it a threat to global food security. Edited by: Sean Sinico https://p.dw.com/p/5PhBC Skip next section Germany's Sky TV won't send staff to F1 race in Qatar 11/20/2026 November 20, 2026 Germany's Sky TV won't send staff to F1 race in Qatar Mark Hallam The last two races of the season, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, have been in considerable doubt all season amid the conflict with Iran and the Houthis in Yemen in the Gulf Image: HOCH ZWEI/picture alliance The German broadcaster Sky TV — not to be confused with the British-based Sky Sports F1 which is the largest English-language commercial F1 broadcaster — will not be sending any staff to the Formula 1 Qatar Grand Prix because of security concerns in connection with the conflict in Iran and the wider Middle East. Sky TV announced the move on Friday, just a week before the contentious race weekend from November 27-29. Sky will broadcast the entire race weekend as usual, but will use global feed images and will not send any of its own staff to Lusail International Circuit. F1 races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia this spring were canceled as the US war with Iran was in its most active phase, with major disruptions to commercial flights. The season-ending double header in Qatar and then the United Arab Emirates a week later has been in serious doubt ever since. Nominally at least, both races are going ahead — and in all likelihood, teams will have already started dispatching equipment and personnel to the region to begin preparations by now. Sky TV said it still planned to send a team to the season finale in Abu Dhabi, just across the Strait of Hormuz from Iran, on December 6. But it said it continued to "monitor developments and assess the situation on an ongoing basis." Edited by: Alex Berry https://p.dw.com/p/5Pg2U Skip next section Germany's electricity exports rise 11/20/2026 November 20, 2026 Germany's electricity exports rise Germany's electricity exports rose in the first three quarters of this year, according to official data released on Friday. According to the energy association BDEW, Germany has been a net importer of electricity since 2023. The neighbouring countries Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands, were the most important buyers of German electricity in the first nine months of 2026. Together, they bought about half of all German electricity exports. The volume of German electricity exported rose by 25.5% compared with the same period last year, to 48.8 terawatt-hours, while its value increased by 51.3% to €4.3 billion ($4.7 billion). Electricity imports into Germany fell by 13.3% in volume, but at 49.2 terawatt-hours they remained slightly above exports. While imported electricity cost an average of €116 per megawatt-hour, 39% more than a year earlier, exported electricity from Germany averaged only €87 per megawatt-hour, some 20.6% more than a year earlier. With a high share of renewable energy sources , wind and solar, Germany tends to offer electricity when supply is high and prices are low, but in times of shortage it has to pay higher prices for imported electricity.
